excerpt: XBOW is an autonomous AI penetration-testing platform that finds and validates vulnerabilities with proof-of-concept exploits. It reached No. 1 on HackerOne's US leaderboard in 2025 and raised a $120M Series C in 2026.
content:
XBOW is an offensive security platform that uses AI to do the work of a penetration tester. Instead of a person probing an application once a year, XBOW runs continuously, simulates real attacks against web applications, and reports only the vulnerabilities it can prove, each with a proof-of-concept exploit and remediation advice. Its site says more than 150 security teams use it, and that it can cover anything from a single application to thousands.

The company was founded by Oege de Moor, according to Help Net Security. It drew wide attention in 2025 when its AI system reached the number one spot on HackerOne's leaderboard, which Help Net Security described as the first time a machine outperformed all the human hackers on the bug-bounty platform. In June 2025 it raised a $75 million Series B led by Altimeter's Apoorv Agrawal, with Sequoia Capital and Nat Friedman participating, bringing its total funding to $117 million.

In March 2026 XBOW announced a $120 million Series C led by DFJ Growth and Northzone, which it said values the company at over $1 billion. Sofina, Alkeon Capital, Altimeter, NFDG Ventures and Sequoia Capital also took part. SecurityWeek reported that the round brought total funding to $237 million and that the money would go towards enterprise and international expansion.

XBOW is sold to security teams, not individuals. Its pricing page says pricing is scoped to each environment and is usage-based, scaling with coverage rather than a fixed annual engagement, and that it can be bought through the AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle and Microsoft marketplaces. No prices are published.

This profile draws on XBOW's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

use_cases: Running continuous penetration tests instead of a yearly manual engagement
Validating vulnerabilities with proof-of-concept exploits before they reach a ticket queue
Covering a large portfolio of web applications without adding security headcount
Buying offensive security testing through an existing cloud marketplace agreement

want findings that come with proof they can be exploited
already buy software through AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle or Microsoft marketplaces

alternatives.intro: Other ways to run offensive security testing. We have not compared them hands-on.

items.name: Horizon3.ai NodeZero
items.what: Autonomous penetration testing for internal and external networks
items.difference: Focuses on network and infrastructure attack paths rather than web applications.

items.name: Pentera
items.difference: Emulates attacks across the internal network and cloud; not AI-agent based in the same way.

items.name: HackerOne
items.what: Bug bounty and human-led pentest marketplace
items.difference: Uses human researchers; XBOW ranked on its leaderboard.

faq.a: It runs autonomous, AI-driven penetration tests on applications and reports vulnerabilities only once it has validated them with a proof-of-concept exploit.

faq.q: How much funding has XBOW raised?
faq.a: $237 million in total, according to SecurityWeek: a $75 million Series B in June 2025 and a $120 million Series C in March 2026 that valued it at over $1 billion.
